- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–2% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model fails to correct; apply downward bias starting at sentiment crossover point.
- Model consistently underestimates mean-reversion periods; add 0.5–1.5% lagged mean adjustment if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is below 10% of 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overconfidence in short-term momentum.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.67 → -0.33 → +0.67), model overfits; apply smoothing filter or reduce forecast volatility by 20%.
